jobs.name: woodland-borough-gritty-v4
jobs.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: revised sci-fi game environment reference, grittier inhabited frontier.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the existing woodland settlement concept. Image 2 is the original GAME SCREENSHOT, supplied solely to preserve the natural environment.
KEEP the current game's trees, individual leaf forms, grass blades, flowers, terrain outside the settlement footprints, sky, daytime illumination, camera framing and major cast shadows. Do not low-poly the forest, remake the terrain, change the season, or hide it behind fog. Keep the foreground tree right of center and its shadow exactly. Maintain the image 1 camera, aspect ratio and placement of the three main buildings, vehicle, people and water equipment. Change the SETTLEMENT'S DESIGN, SURFACES AND SMALL LOCAL GROUND AREAS.
Goal: the user finds the settlement too perfect and wants a grittier lived-in futuristic world, with the industrial, worn frontier feeling they value in Anarchy Online. Make the difference immediately evident in physical design and use, even in the same daylight. This place has had forty years of work, repairs, different owners and uneven funding. People still live and work here; this is functioning advanced infrastructure with tired exteriors.
Break up the matching ivory/teal/orange prefab set. The LEFT workshop is heavier gray-beige concrete and dark steel, with a squat added sheet-metal service annex, a replaced door surround, visible water stains under its vent, and one large patch panel in a mismatched old green paint. Its canopy is a faded patched blue-gray tarp with a shallow sag on two ordinary steel supports. Keep an open working bay, one battered workbench and a couple of reused transport crates.
The CENTER clinic retains a compact prefab shell but has yellowed composite panels, a sun-faded medical marking, painted-over institutional branding, an old service number too worn to read, and a replaced door of a different color. Give its doorway a simple corrugated metal rain hood instead of the matching orange cloth awning, a dull cool-white work light, and mud tracked onto the concrete step.
The RIGHT home is a somewhat older rust-red and dull gray module with a short attached charcoal utility lean-to, a solid battered porch roof, an external junction box and a SINGLE chunky exposed cable in a crude bracketed run. A chair and a little personal planting by the doorway show somebody cares for the place. Avoid symmetrical repeated welcome-light compositions.
Water equipment at far right: pale industrial tanks with faded hazard bands, rust staining specifically at metal straps and seams, mineral runoff below pipe connections, a few replacement brackets and one repainted access panel. The control cabinet is scuffed with an old inspection sticker; a small indicator still works. Pipes remain few, thick and easy to model.
The central yard has compacted dirt, worn wheel ruts, a small muddy patch and a few shallow puddles near the leaking service area. Preserve original foreground flowers and grass except exactly where the footpath passes. Add a couple of concrete repair slabs and a disused panel leaning against a workshop wall. Keep clutter purposeful, sparse and readable, not a garbage field. Residents wear ordinary stained work clothes, with no military hero poses.
Materials: desaturated gray concrete, dirty cream composite, faded industrial green, old oxide red, dark steel. Rust and chipped paint only where materials and use justify them. Broad stains, patched color fields and a few readable seams are sufficient; do not increase geometry complexity with hundreds of greebles. Maintain moderately detailed, smooth-shaded, economical game-ready hard surfaces with modest bevels. This must be achievable through simple modules, material variation, decals and a small prop kit.
Avoid: pristine utopian resort, matched branding and fresh paint, cute toy-like low poly, general sepia filter, changed forest rendering, apocalyptic ruin, collapsed structures, abandonment, dramatic battle damage, excessive neon, ornamental cables everywhere, text captions, borders, watermark.
Output one complete revised landscape scene. Preserve the source's lighting and environment; make the grit come from the inhabited built world.
